Fixed in `app.py`: a bad `day` now gets a 400 with a JSON error instead of reaching `trips.summary` and raising. I ran the handler directly against both logged cases and a few others; there's no test suite in the project, so nothing permanent was added.

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `day=2026-09-31` | 400 `day '2026-09-31' is not a real calendar date` |
| `day=14/09/2026` | 400 `day '14/09/2026' is not in YYYY-MM-DD format` |
| `day=` or no `day` at all | 400 `day is required, as YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `day=2026-09-14` | 200, same summary as before |

The missing/empty `day` case was also a 500 before, so I covered it with the same check.

Python's ISO parser also accepts compact forms like `day=20260914`. Those returned 200 before and still do; I left that alone rather than start rejecting requests that currently work. If you want strictly `YYYY-MM-DD`, it's a one-line tightening.

The date picker is still sending these values, so the dashboard will now show a 400 instead of a 500 until that's fixed on its side.
